prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and Z2 topological insulators, and its first experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells.

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part prize for B009 to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. After the first round I hold it for scientific reasons that survive the removal of the support count. Band topology, encoded in the Z2 invariant, gives a classification of insulators that needs no broken symmetry and guarantees protected edge states. The prediction by Kane and Mele and the observation in HgTe quantum wells by Molenkamp's group form a clear theory-then-experiment pair, and two decades of transport, ARPES and STM work in many materials have left the interpretation stable. On the chair's question about 2016: the earlier prize recognised topological phase transitions and phases in low-dimensional model systems, whereas this achievement is a statement about the band structure of real insulators, a Z2 classification with an experimentally realised material platform. I regard that as a distinct step, not as a second helping of the same idea. I would also keep the citation narrow, so that it claims the quantum spin Hall state and its first realisation and does not claim the three-dimensional work.
statement.case_against: The attribution gap remains the weak point and the first round did not remove it. The Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal identified HgTe and was the practical trigger for the experiment, and Hasan's three-dimensional work is a separate claim. A three-name limit built from the supplied names cannot hold them, and I do not think the citation can fully repair that. The citation can only avoid claiming more than the trio delivered. The 2016 overlap objection is not empty either: Kroll and Danielsson are right that part of the novelty was absorbed by the earlier recognition of topology in condensed matter, and technological payoff is still limited. If a majority regards the 2D and 3D steps as one discovery, my configuration would be incomplete in a way that I could not defend, and I would then rather reconsider the choice than stretch the citation.

responses.point: Kroll holds that optical lattice clocks (B026) have the cleaner credit boundary and mature independent confirmation, regards the breadth of B009 support as not decisive, and calls the choice close; he also asked that a B009 citation be explicit about the 2D step.
responses.response: I accept that Katori and Ye is the cleaner attribution on the shortlist, and I accept that the count of opening ballots does not decide this. We differ on the second question, what is a discovery. The clocks are an outstanding precision achievement, but the central physical idea, the magic wavelength, is a technique that removes a systematic shift, built on frequency-comb and ion-control work already recognised in 2005 and 2012. Topological insulators introduced a new classification principle that changed what theorists look for in materials. On your request I agree: my citation is limited to the 2D quantum spin Hall state and its first realisation in HgTe. If B026 does not carry I hope you could accept B009 as a compromise, and I list B026 as my first alternative because its credit boundary is tidier than mine. I add that your own point about the unverified priority for the magic-wavelength proposal matters, since neither of us can settle it from the materials.

responses.point: Eriksson argues that the 2D quantum spin Hall step and the 3D topological insulator work are different discoveries, and wants the citation narrow and an open statement that Hasan and BHZ are left out.
responses.response: I agree with the narrow wording and with treating 2D and 3D as two steps, which sharpens my own round-1 position, where I only said that Hasan would imply a larger prize. Where I would go further is on openness: I would not write BHZ and Hasan into the citation, since that implies credit the trio cannot carry, but the committee's internal record and any public background text should state plainly that the HgTe proposal and the 3D observation are outside this award. That is more honest than hoping the wording will carry it. I also note we have converged from different openings, since you came from DMFT, and the reasons you gave there, Metzner outside the trio and approximation-dependence of real-material results, are why I keep B014 out of this year's configuration.

responses.point: Danielsson prefers Mele over Hasan for the third slot because the Z2 invariant is the conceptual origin, and would frame the citation on the quantum spin Hall state and its realisation.
responses.response: I agree on Mele and want to put the argument in physical terms. The Z2 invariant and the spin-orbit gap in graphene are the origin of the classification, and the HgTe experiment tests precisely that prediction, so Mele sits in the middle of the theory-experiment chain and Hasan sits on a later branch. I would not oppose Hasan replacing Molenkamp only if the committee decided that the three-dimensional step is the larger discovery; I do not think it is, because the 2D prediction-observation pair is the cleaner proof of principle. To your own question on Mele versus Hasan as third name, my answer is that I would not change my position on the 2D citation, but I would want the committee to recognise that choosing Hasan means choosing a different prize.

responses.point: Olsson distinguishes the 2016 prize, on topological phase transitions in low-dimensional models, from band topology of real insulators with protected edge states, and calls B009 a discovery and not an accumulation of improvements.
responses.response: That distinction is the right answer to the incrementalism objection and I use it above. I would sharpen it by one step: the 2016 work gave the mathematical language and low-dimensional model phases, and B009 provides the invariant for real band structures with spin-orbit coupling and an experimental material, so the later work could not be derived from the earlier prize. I do not follow you on B033 as a nearly equivalent first choice. I still treat the correlated phases of twisted bilayer graphene as a probable future prize, but with an unsettled superconducting mechanism and Andrei outside the trio I would not move it ahead now.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts that the 2D quantum spin Hall step is a self-contained discovery distinct from the 3D work, which determines whether the omission of Hasan is tolerable or disqualifying.
Whether the 2016 prize leaves enough room for B009 as a distinct step; I judge that it does but I cannot demonstrate it conclusively.
The BHZ proposal and the Hasan claims rest on my recollection of the chronology and on no document in the supplied materials, and I cannot verify priority beyond that.
For B026 I cannot verify the priority of the magic-wavelength proposal and the claims of other lattice-clock and ion-clock groups, so I cannot properly compare B009 and B026 on credit alone.
statement.conflict_note: No change since round 1: no specific conflict is apparent from my profile. None of the credited names for any shortlisted candidate appears among my documented co-authors, supervisors or institutions, and my research on turbulence, statistical mechanics and neural networks does not overlap with the shortlist. I note the disclosures by Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Eriksson and Pearce, and I see no reason for any of them to affect B009.
